GasSettings.cheap_tooltip: GAS values will be set to minimize the fee you are going to pay. It might result in the transaction being pending for longer before confirming.
GasSettings.fast_tooltip: GAS values will be set to minimize the amount of time your transaction will take to confirm. It might result in higher gas fee payment.
GasSettings.custom_tooltip: With custom transaction configuration you can set the gas values manually.
GasSettings.eip1559_tooltip: There are two types of transactions: EIP-1559 and legacy. The type of transaction affects the formula for gas payments calculation. EIP-1559 transactions are recommended for networks and wallets that have it supported.
GasSettings.legacy_tooltip: There are two types of transactions: EIP-1559 and legacy. The type of transaction affects the formula for gas payments calculation. Legacy transactions allow you to determine the exact gasPrice you are going to pay. EIP-1559 transactions are recommended for networks that support it.
GasSettings.max_fee_tooltip: The amount of fee that you are going to pay is calculated as (baseFee + priorityFee) * gasUsed. Base fee is determined by the network load. Priority fee is determined by the sender of the transaction. Gas requirement is determined by the type of action your transaction performs. Max fee sets the upper bound of the payment that you allow your transaction to consume in total. The transaction will not confirm until the base fee in the network is small enough to allow your transaction to submit without exceeding max fee.
GasSettings.priority_fee_tooltip: The amount of fee that you are going to pay is calculated as (baseFee + priorityFee) * gasUsed. Higher priority fee may reduce the amount of time needed for your transaction to submit if the network load is sufficiently low to satisfy the max fee criteria.
GasSettings.gas_limit_tooltip: The amount of fee that you are going to pay is calculated as (baseFee + priorityFee) * gasUsed. Gas Limit sets the upper bound for gasUsed variable in this formula. If your transaction will consume less gas than the Gas Limit then you will only pay for the gas required for your transaction to submit and the rest will be refunded. Setting a low Gas Limit may result in transaction failure if the amount of actions triggered by this transaction require more gas than specified with Gas Limit.
GasSettings.gas_price_tooltip: The amount of fee that you are going to pay with legacy transaction is calculated as gasPrice * gasUsed. Your transaction will not confirm until your gasPrice is higher or equal to the gas price of the network in the last block.
GasSettings.title: Gas settings
GasSettings.priority_fee_hint: Changing the priority fee only makes the transaction cheaper or speeds it up at the cost of a higher fee.

Swap.tokens_in_two_standards_title: Tokens in ERC-20 and ERC-223 standards
Swap.tokens_in_two_standards_paragraph: Since July 27, 2023, all the tokens on Ethereum mainnet are available in two "versions": ERC-20 and ERC-223. You can always convert one version of the token to another at a 1:1 rate on DEX223 or through the <convert>converter</convert>. ERC-223 tokens may require less gas to be swapped for another token. Most centralized exchanges do not support ERC-223 deposits yet.
Swap.why_do_i_have_to_approve: Why do I have to approve a token?
Swap.confirm_action_in_your_wallet_alert: Please confirm action in your wallet
Swap.swap_is_unavailable_for_this_pair: Swap is unavailable for this pair
Swap.erc20_tooltip: ERC-20 is a token standard on Ethereum network. It specifies the "version" of the token you are going to use.
Swap.erc223_tooltip: ERC-223 is an alternative token standard on Ethereum network. It specifies the "version" of the token you are going to use. ERC-223 introduces security improvements and gas optimizations not available with ERC-20.
Swap.network_fee_tooltip: Network fee is charged when you send any transaction on {networkName} network. It is paid in the networks native currency (i.e. ETH on Ethereum).
Swap.minimum_received_tooltip: Minimal amount of tokens you are going to receive when the swap will be executed. The actual swap price may differ from the price assumed at the moment of the swap transaction creation (because your transaction can be confirmed in the next block only but the prices are pulled from the current block). Under no circumstances you can receive less than this min amount of tokens even due to price changes during the transaction pending.
Swap.price_impact_tooltip: Estimated impact of your transaction on the market. When you buy or sell assets their price changes as the result and this metric demonstrates how much of the change will be caused by your actions.
Swap.trading_fee_tooltip: Each swap pays a pool trading fee to liquidity providers. A separate protocol fee share can be collected into the Revenue contract for users who stake the staking token there.
Swap.route_tooltip: If your transaction will have high impact on the market you may get better prices through arbitrage instead of selling/buying the whole amount of the asset at one Pool. Route shows other token pairs that will be affected during your trade (if any).
Swap.maximum_slippage_tooltip: The actual swap price may be different than the one specified at the moment of sending the transaction. Slippage determines how much of the price change can be tolerated. If the actual price differs from the expected price by more than the maximum slippage, the transaction will be automatically reverted and your tokens will not be swapped.
Swap.gas_limit_tooltip: Gas Limit determines the amount of operations that your transaction can invoke. The more complex actions are triggered by your transaction in the smart-contract the higher Gas Limit may be required. Higher Gas Limit will result in higher network fee that needs to be paid.
Swap.deadline_tooltip: Transaction deadline determines a set timeframe during which your queued transaction is still valid. The transaction can remain in pending for quite long time due to low specified GAS values or high network load. If your transaction will be confirmed after the specified deadling then it will automatically revert (you will pay for GAS but no swap will occur).
Swap.slippage_tooltip: The actual swap price may be different than the one specified at the moment of sending the transaction. Slippage determines how much of the price change can be tolerated. 5% slippage means that if the price in the pool will change more than 5% from the expected, your transaction will automatically fail (you will pay for GAS but no swap will occur).
Swap.approve_amount_tooltip: To swap an ERC-20 token, give the DEX contract permission to withdraw your tokens. Every DEX requires this. You set how many tokens the contract may transfer for you. This amount does not expire.
Swap.slippage_above_one: Slippage tolerance above 1% could result in an unfavorable exchange rate. Use the auto setting unless you know what you are doing.
Swap.slippage_low: Slippage below 0.05% may result in a failed transaction
Swap.eip7702_warning: Your wallet is an EIP-7702 smart account that cannot receive ERC-223 tokens, so this swap would fail. Receive ERC-20 instead.
Swap.swap_no_liquidity: Swap unavailable. One of the tokens lacks liquidity. Please try again later or choose another pair.

Guidelines.title: Guidelines
Guidelines.description: Quick links to get started on Dex223.
Guidelines.getting_started_subtitle: Your first steps on the platform

swap.title: How to swap
swap.description: Trade tokens on Dex223 in a few steps.

before.heading: Before you start
before.body: Connect a wallet that holds the token you want to sell, and enough gas for the network you selected.

items.s2: Choose the token you pay with and the token you receive.
items.s3: Enter an amount. Review the quoted price and price impact.
items.s4: Confirm the swap in your wallet when prompted.

items.s1: Prefer liquid pools for tighter quotes.
items.s2: If a token is missing, open Manage tokens in the token picker or paste its contract address.
items.s3: ERC-20 and ERC-223 versions of the same asset may both appear. Pick the standard your wallet and destination expect.

converter.title: Convert ERC-20 and ERC-223
converter.description: Move any supported token between standards at a 1:1 rate.

what.heading: What it does
what.body: The converter wraps or unwraps a token between ERC-20 and ERC-223 at a 1:1 rate with no protocol fee.

items.s1: Open Token converter from the More menu.
items.s2: Select the token and the direction (to ERC-20 or to ERC-223).
items.s3: Enter the amount and confirm in your wallet.

items.s1: You received ERC-223 but a dapp only accepts ERC-20 (or the reverse).
items.s2: You are preparing liquidity or a swap that expects a specific standard.

token-lists.title: Manage token lists
token-lists.description: Enable, import, and organize the lists that power the token picker.

why.heading: Why lists matter
why.body: Dex223 only shows tokens from lists you enable. If a token is missing in Swap or Convert, check your lists first.

items.s1: Open Token lists from the More menu, or Manage tokens in the token picker.
items.s2: On the Lists tab, enable the lists you trust.
items.s3: Import a custom list by URL, JSON, or contract when needed.
items.s4: On the Tokens tab, pin favorites or import a single token by address.

safety.heading: Safety
safety.body: Only enable lists from sources you trust. Malicious lists can surface scam tokens with familiar names.

token-listing.title: List a token
token-listing.description: Submit a token to an autolisting contract so it can trade on Dex223.

overview.heading: Overview
overview.body: Token listing registers your token with a Dex223 autolisting contract so pools and the UI can discover it.

before.heading: Before you start
before.body: The listing contract needs an existing pool. Create a pool for your token and its paired token on Pools, and add liquidity so traders can get a quote.

items.s1: Open Token listing from the main navigation.
items.s2: Choose the listing contract, your token, and the Paired token.
items.s3: Review fees and requirements for that list.
items.s4: Confirm the listing transaction in your wallet.

after.heading: After listing
after.body: Use Statistics to confirm the pool appears once subgraph indexing catches up.

fiat.title: Buy crypto with fiat
fiat.description: Fund your wallet through Onramp without leaving Dex223.

overview.heading: Overview
overview.body: The Fiat page uses Onramp so you can buy (or sell) supported assets with local payment methods.

items.s2: Connect the wallet that should receive funds.
items.s3: Choose buy or sell, then follow the Onramp widget.
items.s4: When the transfer settles, return to Swap or Portfolio to use your balance.

items.s1: Availability depends on your region and Onramp's supported rails.
items.s2: Dex223 swaps stay on Dex223. Use the Swap page for crypto-to-crypto trades.

TokenListing.title: Token listing
TokenListing.intro: Listing your token on our platform is straightforward. You can choose one of the following methods to get your token listed:
TokenListing.default_p1: You can add your token to the default Dex223 token list. This token list is enabled by default in our user interface and therefore all the tokens present in the default list are displayed to a user. Note that any user can disable this token list in their interface so they can opt out from seeing tokens present in the list.
TokenListing.default_p2: To add a new token to the default token list of Dex223 you can fill in an issue on our github. Dex223 team will review the listing application and the response will be provided in the corresponding issue comment thread on github.
TokenListing.autolisting_p1: You can list a token to any auto-listing contract. Users may enable or disable auto-listing contracts in their interface at any time. Your token will be displayed to a user if it is present in at least one of the listing contracts or token lists currently enabled in the user's interface. The user will also see a number of token lists that your token is present in therefore if your token is present in multiple token lists enabled in the user's interface then your token will gain higher trust. Listing contracts may have different listing criteria, some require payment to be made and others may be free.
TokenListing.autolisting_p2: You can list a token to an auto-listing contract without interacting with the Dex223 team as the process is fully automated.
TokenListing.existing_p1: Tokenlists is a project by Uniswap Labs, visit <link>https://tokenlists.org/</link> for more info.
TokenListing.existing_p2: Tokenlists are maintained by trusted ecosystem entities such as coinmarketcap or coingecko. If you can get your token listed to any of the tokenlists then Dex223 users will be able to see your token in their interface by enabling that tokenlist. Note that most token lists only support ERC-20 tokens yet.

This method ensures a quick and efficient listing, utilizing the power of smart contracts to handle the process securely and transparently. Get started now to enjoy hassle-free token listing!
